headline.text: Asked for a bare result, then for options and a way back

observations.text: In a routine test result, the user asked only to be told whether it passed.
In project planning, the user asked to see alternatives and what is given up before deciding. In a high-risk migration, the user asked for failure cases and a way back before approving.
In the next session relative to J4, the user said they do not always want short answers. They said they want enough to judge what to do.

interpretation.text: In these records, the user asked for little in a routine check and for more before a decision or approval. This fits their own words in J5 about wanting enough to judge. It is tentative and limited to these situations.

alternative: The difference may come from what the user already knew in each case. They may have had the routine test context, but not the migration risks. The task type may matter less than that.
limitation: The records do not say what the user already knew in each situation. They also do not show the answers given, so we cannot tell whether the requested detail was enough.
